title: Longer Contiguous Segments of Ones than Zeros
summary: Given a binary string, determine if the longest sequence of 1's is strictly longer than the longest sequence of 0's.
statement: Given a binary string, determine if the longest sequence of 1's is strictly longer than the longest sequence of 0's. If not, return false. If there are no 0's, the longest sequence of 0's is considered 0. The same rule applies for 1's.
constraints: Compare the longest contiguous runs; the run of ones must be strictly longer.
hints: Track current and maximum run lengths separately for zero and one.
Extend the matching run and reset the other run at every character.
After the scan, compare the two maximums with a strict greater-than test.
Every maximal run ends either at a different character or at the string boundary, and its length is recorded before comparison.
editorial: Every maximal run ends either at a different character or at the string boundary, and its length is recorded before comparison.

tests.explanation: The longest one-run has length two while the longest zero-run has length one.
Both longest runs have length three, so the strict comparison is false.
